summary.name: IconCraft
summary.one_liner: IconCraft is a free, open-source macOS utility that lets you change any app's displayed name and icon to a look you prefer, while leaving the underlying app unchanged and reversible.
keywords: windows linux icon customizer coming soon
use_cases: Give a replacement app the icon of the app you used before
Set default apps for browser, email and PDFs in one list
Rename or re-skin AI-built tools with custom icons
Bulk-replace icons across a folder of similar apps
summary.what_it_does: IconCraft changes the name and icon shown for macOS apps, including Apple's own, using either genuine original icons found on the Mac or any image you supply. It lists apps from common folders such as the home folder, Setapp and external drives, with search (⌘K), grouping, sorting and bulk replacement. It consolidates eleven default-app settings (browser, email, PDF, photos, video and more) into a single list. Every change is journaled before it is made, so individual apps or everything can be restored, and a background keeper reapplies skins after app updates. It runs at login from the menu bar.
notable: Journaled changes with one-click restore per app or for all apps
Consolidates eleven macOS default-app settings into one list
Does not request Full Disk Access, Accessibility or Screen Recording, per the page
Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple; MIT licensed; Homebrew cask install
caveats: Windows and Linux versions are in development and not yet released
Changing another app's icon or name writes inside that app's bundle, which macOS App Management guards
